h1: Hydraulic press brakes — CNC, hybrid and NC, 33 to 1,323 US tons
intro: A hydraulic press brake bends sheet and plate between a punch and a V-die with two hydraulic cylinders, giving full force over the whole stroke at the lowest price per ton — the machine for plate, long parts and production. NovoTech sells three kinds in Canada, all on this page: CNC hydraulic press brakes with linear scales, servo valves, crowning and a graphic control — the premium Dener XL in 18 models from 66 to 661 US tons and 5 to 20 ft, and NovoTech's own value line from 55 to 331 tons, heavy-duty and tandem to 1,323 tons and 26 ft; hybrid press brakes — the mild hybrid servo motor and pump, an option on every XL that cuts energy by 42 – 58 %, and Dener's XH full hybrid; and NC torsion-bar press brakes from 33 to 441 tons for repeat parts in one material. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, and is installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For a brake with no hydraulic oil see the electric press brakes; for 33 – 66 ton machines over 4 – 5 ft, the compact press brakes.

faq.q: CNC, hybrid or NC — which hydraulic press brake do I need?
faq.a: A CNC brake measures the ram on linear scales and corrects it through servo valves, calculates the bend from the drawing, crowns the bed and changes material in the program — the machine for mixed work, tight angles and multi-bend parts, and the one most Canadian shops buy. The hybrid is a CNC brake with a servo pump: it costs a little more and pays it back in power, speed and noise when the brake runs all day. An NC brake positions the back gauge and the ram depth from a stored program with the cylinders kept in step by a torsion bar — rigid, cheap to maintain, right for the same parts in one material every day. For 4 – 7 ft work in sheet up to 8 ga, where a 100-ton machine is more than you need, see the compact press brakes.

The premium Dener XL and XH are built in Turkey on the heaviest frame, with ESA or Delem controls, back gauges to 6 axes, sheet followers, robot cells and Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada — the machines for plate, 3/8″ and 1/2″ over 10 to 20 ft, two shifts, a long options list. NovoTech's value line is the same architecture — monoblock frame, Hawe servo valves, linear scales, Delem control — built in China to our specification at about two-thirds of the price: the right buy for a job shop that needs a 100 – 300 ton CNC brake or an NC brake for repeat parts, and the only line that goes to 1,323 tons and 26 ft. Both are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians.

faq.q: How much tonnage and length do I need?
faq.a: Air bending takes F = S² × 2 × R ÷ (1.4 × V) tonnes per metre of bend — the sheet thickness S and the V opening V in millimetres, the tensile strength R = 47 kg/mm² for mild steel (70 for stainless, 25 for aluminum), the formula behind the EUROSTAMP and Dener bending charts; in inches and US tons per foot it reads 575 × t² ÷ V. With the standard V of about 8 × the thickness, 3 mm needs about 24 t/m (8 US tons per foot), 6 mm 48 t/m (16), 1/4″ 54 t/m (18), 3/8″ in a 3″ V 80 t/m (27) and 1/2″ in a 5″ V 85 t/m (29). Multiply by the bend length and add about 20 % in reserve: 3 m × 6 mm is a 175-ton press brake, 10 ft × 1/4″ a 200 – 220 US ton machine, 10 ft × 3/8″ a 300 – 320 ton machine and 13 ft × 1/2″ a 400 – 450 ton machine. The tonnage calculator in the buying guide on the press brake page does the arithmetic for your thickness and length; tell us your thickest and longest bend and we size the brake and the tooling.

faq.q: What is a hybrid press brake?
faq.a: On a conventional hydraulic brake the motor and pump run at full speed all day, whether the ram moves or not. A hybrid drives the hydraulics with servo motors, so the pump turns only while the ram moves, at the speed the ram needs. Dener builds it two ways. The mild hybrid, an option on every XL, keeps the XL's hydraulic circuit and replaces only the AC motor and fixed pump with a servo motor and servo pump: Dener measures 42 – 58 % energy saving and 17 – 75 % faster approach and return against the standard XL, with less heat in the oil and a quieter shop, and everything else — frame, cylinders, valves, tooling, controls — is the XL. The XH is the full hybrid, a series designed around its servo-driven hydraulics. On NovoTech's value line, every WAD CNC brake has the mild hybrid drive as standard.

faq.q: Which control comes with the machine?
faq.a: The premium XL comes with the 15″ ESA S840 2D graphic touch-screen control (Delem DA-66S / 69S and the ESA S875 W 3D control are options): draw the profile, the control calculates the bend sequence, tonnage, back-gauge positions and crowning. The value-line CNC brakes come with the 15″ Delem DA-53Tx — the 18.5″ DA-58Tx (2D graphic), the 24″ DA-66S and DA-69S, the ESA S840 and S875 W, the Cybelec CybTouch 12 and the SCS920 are options; the NC brakes with the Estun E21PS (E315PS, Delem DA-41T or ESA S630 as options). All program in inches or millimetres, and the buying guide on the press brake page compares every one of them.

faq.q: What back gauge and axes are available?
faq.a: Every CNC machine has the Y1 and Y2 ram axes and an X back-gauge axis on a ball screw and linear guides. Options go up to the 6-axis gauge with X1, X2, R1, R2, Z1 and Z2 — two independently positioned fingers for angled flanges — plus a CNC crowning axis; the NC brakes have X and the depth stop. The back gauge is set by the control for every bend of the program.

faq.q: What tooling fits, and do you stock it?
faq.a: European-style (Promecam / Amada) segmented tooling fits every line: the premium Dener brakes carry European-style top-tool holders, the value-line brakes their own clamping, and a sectioned punch set with a 2-V or 4-V die ships with every machine (a 4-V die with the Dener brakes, a 2-V die with the value line) — tell us which tooling standard your shop already has and we fit the holders to match. NovoTech stocks Eurostamp press brake tooling in Canada — punches, dies, radius, hemming and joggle tools, gooseneck and special profiles — and sizes it to your machine; quick-release, pneumatic and Wila hydraulic clamping and American-style adapters are options, not standard equipment.

faq.q: What about safety and the Ontario pre-start review?
faq.a: Side guards, an enclosed rear guard, interlocked doors and an anti-panic foot pedal with emergency stop are standard; DSP or Fiessler laser finger protection and light curtains are options we recommend for every CNC machine. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — NovoTech sells, installs and supports press brakes across Canada and the United States. Installation, commissioning and operator training are free of charge in the Greater Toronto Area; outside the GTA our technicians do the same work at an additional charge. Dener Canada and NovoTech stock the parts in Canada. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.

faq.q: What does delivery cost, and who unloads the machine?
faq.a: A press brake ordered from the factory (back-ordered) travels in its container straight from the port, customs and the rail yard to your plant door: in the Greater Toronto Area that delivery is free; outside the GTA the freight is quoted and charged. A machine from NovoTech's stock is loaded, shipped and unloaded at the buyer's cost. In every case unloading is the buyer's responsibility and expense — the crane or forklift, the rigging and moving the machine onto its foundation — so book a rigger for the delivery day; we are glad to recommend riggers who know press brakes and to tell you the weight and lifting points.

No — the hydraulic oil is bought by the customer. Before commissioning, fill the tank with ISO VG 46 anti-wear hydraulic oil (AW 46) in the quantity shown in the specification table for your model; our technician checks the level and bleeds the system during installation. Electric press brakes have no hydraulic oil at all.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
